newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares mixed over fears of Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares mixed over fears of Fed rate hike.

text.p: Russian shares were mixed on Monday over fears of an interest rate hike tomorrow by the U.S. Federal Reserve, traders said.

"People are waiting to hear what (Federal Reserve chairman) Alan Greenspan will say tomorrow," said Igor Lossavio, head of overseas operations at Prospekt. "It's already having an effect on the market."
The Russian Trading System's 23-share index closed at 310.44, easing from a midday high of 314.54 but slightly above Friday's close of 309.41.

Megionneftegaz, a production unit of oil holding company Slavneft, lost almost nine percent during the day after news that it would not issue American Depositary Receipts in the first quarter as expected.
But it rallied in the afternoon to close at $5.71 on about $798,000 traded, down slightly from Friday's close of $5.90.
"All eyes are looking that way (at the Fed) at the moment. The only buyers are domestic Russian investors," said Peter Kizenko, chief equities trader at ING Barings.
But traders also said investors were showing interest in second-tier shares.

"Second tiers continue to hold," Kizenko said. "The stock got up so quickly when it was first offered that there was not much trading and there were a lot of unsatisfied buyers. And they know that the stock will not be available when the market turns again."
Samarenergo closed at $0.610 on a volume of $107,386, up from $0.510 at its last close on March 19.
Traders said the lower prices were also due to the approaching end of the financial quarter.
"Funds are waiting for new money at the beginning of the new financial quarter," Prospekt's Lossavio said.
